messages:
Jordan (PM): quick one — we need to pick a prioritization + rollout approach for the Dedicated model-selection feature. customers asking for per-tenant model pinning + canary sequencing. do we treat this as a single big initiative or split into a quick canary-first experiment + follow-on polish?
Ana (product): +1 to splitting. fewer assumptions if we ship a canary path first. we can validate impact on latency/cost per-tenant.
Mike (eng): agree. from infra side the risky bits are routing and fallback logic. smaller canary reduces blast radius. effort estimate: canary plumbing ~2 sprint dev + testing, full rollout UI + policy ~3 more.
Sofia (ML): also want to be able to route to quantized variants automatically during canary. that reduces cost impact. if we roll without that, customers will hit higher token costs and we'll get noise in quality metrics.
Ravi (ops): ops note — any canary has to include revert controls, alerting, and a staged bump window. otherwise we pay full SRE cycles during rollout. estimate: runbook + dashboards ~1 sprint.
Jordan (PM): thinking in prioritization frameworks: RICE numbers look like this for the two options. canary-first: Reach=4, Impact=3, Confidence=70, Effort=3 -> RICE ~ (4*3*0.7)/3 = 2.8. full-launch-first: Reach=5, Impact=4, Confidence=40, Effort=8 -> RICE ~ (5*4*0.4)/8 = 1.0. rough but shows canary-first wins.
Ana (product): those are reasonable. also consider sequencing benefits: canary generates metrics to de-risk the larger launch.
Mike (eng): tradeoff debate: canary-first means two integrations for infra (canary path + final policy). more total dev flow but lower risk. single big launch is simpler productwise but risky.
Sofia (ML): experimental plan suggestion: 1) canary with 5% of traffic across 3 customer segments 2) collect latency, cost-per-token, quality regressions on eval prompts 3) automatic fallback policy when latency > X or quality delta > Y.
Jordan (PM): +1. propose gating criteria for canary->ramp: - latency p95 <= 20% above baseline - cost per token delta <= 15% - no quality regression on top 10 customer prompts (alpha=0.05). if any fail, rollback.
Ravi (ops): implement canary window: 72h minimum, with automated rollback if metric crosses threshold for 15m. also add an emergency cutoff in console.
Mike (eng): draft rollout config snippet i can implement:
```
canary: {
  percent: 5,
  segments: ["enterprise", "mid-market", "self-serve"],
  health_checks: ["latency_p95", "token_cost", "eval_quality"],
  rollback_rules: {
    latency_p95: {threshold: 1.2, duration: 15m},
    eval_quality: {delta: -0.03, duration: 15m}
  }
}
```
Jordan (PM): nice. question for prioritization: do we need a customer pilot gating (handshake) before canary? some enterprise customers want opt-in.
Ana (product): yes, require explicit opt-in for any tenant-level pinning until we finish compliance review. canary can run on opt-in tenants + small internal beta.
Sofia (ML): also suggest we add a monitoring eval set (10 queries/customer) for automated quality checks. that'll help confidence.
Ravi (ops): ops will own the runbook and the automated rollback. can we push a conservative default: canary percent=2 for first 24h then 5%?
Mike (eng): doable. engineering estimate moves to 3 sprints if we include staged bump logic. still cheaper than one 8-sprint big-bang.
Jordan (PM): decision proposal: prioritize canary-first as a separate MVP initiative. acceptance criteria: canary infra + fallback + dashboards + opt-in pilot customers + documented runbook. afterwards, schedule full policy/UI in next quarterly plan. anyone object?
Ana (product): no objections. please add RICE scoring and acceptance criteria to the ticket.
Mike (eng): I'll scope and attach a tech design doc.
Sofia (ML): I'll prepare the eval prompts and quality thresholds.
Ravi (ops): ops runbook and alerting on my plate.
deploy-bot: new ticket created: #RD-2243 — dedicated-model-canary-mvp (assigned: Mike).
Jordan (PM): thanks — will update roadmap and ping stakeholders. :thumbsup:
